package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised at the source code level to include a sophisticated backdoor (SUNBURST), which was compiled, signed, and distributed as a legitimate update through the official SolarWinds patch management system. This allowed attackers to gain persistent, covert access to thousands of organizations' networks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service startup, the code checks for security tools and sandbox environments, waits a random interval to evade detection, then contacts a remote command-and-control (C2) domain to receive further instructions or payloads, enabling persistent remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs environment checks to evade sandboxes, delays execution to avoid detection, and initiates outbound network connections to attacker-controlled domains, which is not expected in legitimate monitoring software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal SolarWinds Orion code should not perform anti-analysis checks, random execution delays, or contact unknown external domains for instructions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may check for debuggers or sandboxes for licensing or anti-piracy, but not in this context or with this network behavior.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to SolarWinds source code repository and inserts backdoor logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor is compiled and signed as part of legitimate update.

attack_chain.action: Compromised update is distributed to customers via official patch management system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is deployed in thousands of customer environments.

attack_chain.action: On service startup, backdoor code checks for safe execution environment, delays, and contacts C2.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes covert remote access for attacker.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues commands or delivers additional payloads to compromised systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise and lateral movement within victim networks.

behavioral_signatures: Randomized execution delays before network activity
Unexpected outbound connections to newly registered or suspicious domains
Dynamic code execution or payload download in a monitoring tool
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in signed binaries (e.g., SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll)
Presence of obfuscated or anti-analysis logic in production code
Unexplained new DLLs or code blocks in update packages
network_indicators: Connections to known SUNBURST C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud[.]com)
DNS queries to algorithmically generated or recently registered domains
Unusual HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to external IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers, especially to suspicious or recently registered domains. Analyze update packages and binaries for anti-analysis logic, randomized delays, and code that downloads or executes remote payloads. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes in signed binaries. Employ advanced static and behavioral analysis to identify hidden backdoors or anomalous code paths in software updates.
